Do the following using the steps provided in their respective sections.
        Steps:
        1. clone the repo git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
        2. analyse the contents of the repo and create following.
            2.1 create/update dockerfile based on the analysis. 
            2.2 kubernetes yamls based on the analysis.
            2.3 github actions file to build application on pushing to main branch.
        3. add all changed file to git changes 
        4. commit / push to repo

function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a **step‑by‑step guide** that you can copy‑paste into a terminal (or run as a shell script) to finish the task.  
I’ve also included the exact file contents that will be created.

> **NOTE** – The `create_a_docker_file` and `create_kubernetes_yaml_file` helpers are meant for Python projects, so I’m writing the Dockerfile and Kubernetes YAML manually.  
> If you prefer to use the helpers, you can adapt them to your own base image and image name.

---

## 1️⃣ Clone the repository

```bash
git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

---

## 2️⃣ Analyse the repo & create artefacts

### 2.1 Dockerfile

Create a file named `Dockerfile` in the repo root with the following content:

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile
# ------------------------------------
# Base image – choose the latest LTS Node version
FROM node:18-alpine

# Working directory inside the container
WORKDIR /app

# Copy package files first to leverage Docker cache
COPY package*.json ./

# Install production dependencies only
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy the rest of the source code
COPY . .

# Expose the port your app listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Default command
CMD ["node", "app.js"]
```

> **Why this Dockerfile?**  
> * `node:18-alpine` is small, secure, and contains the Node runtime.  
> * `npm ci` guarantees a reproducible install.  
> * Exposing port `3000` matches the typical Express/Node default.

---

### 2.2 Kubernetes YAML

Create a file named `k8s-nodejs-welcome.yaml` (or any name you like) in the repo root with the following content:

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: yourdockerhub/nodejs-welcome:latest   # <-- replace with your image
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80
    targetPort: 3000
```

> **What this does**  
> * Deploys two replicas of your app.  
> * Exposes the app via a `ClusterIP` service on port `80`, forwarding to container port `3000`.  
> * Replace `yourdockerhub/nodejs-welcome:latest` with the actual image you’ll push.

---

### 2.3 GitHub Actions workflow

Create a directory `.github/workflows` (if it doesn’t exist) and add a file called `docker-image.yml` with the following content:

```yaml
name: Build and Push Docker image

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v3

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v2

      - name: Log in to Docker Hub
        uses: docker/login-action@v2
        with:
          username: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}
          password: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Build and push Docker image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
        with:
          context: .
          push: true
          tags: yourdockerhub/nodejs-welcome:latest   # <-- replace with your image
```

> **How it works**  
> * Triggers on pushes to `main`.  
> * Builds the Docker image from the repo root (`context: .`).  
> * Pushes the image to Docker Hub (or any registry you configure).  
> * Requires two repository secrets: `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME` and `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN`.

---

## 3️⃣ Add the new files to Git

```bash
git add Dockerfile k8s-nodejs-welcome.yaml .github/workflows/docker-image.yml
```

---

## 4️⃣ Commit & push

```bash
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, Kubernetes YAML, and GitHub Actions workflow"
git push origin main
```

---

### Quick sanity check

After pushing, you should see:

* A new **Actions** tab with a successful run of the workflow.  
* In your Docker registry, an image tagged `latest`.  
* If you apply the Kubernetes YAML (`kubectl apply -f k8s-nodejs-welcome.yaml`) you’ll get two pods running and a service exposing port 80.

---

### What to replace

| Placeholder | What to replace it with |
|-------------|------------------------|
| `yourdockerhub/nodejs-welcome:latest` | Your Docker Hub (or other registry) image name, e.g. `zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest` |
| `yourdockerhub` | Your Docker Hub username or registry URL |
| `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME` & `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` | Repository secrets set in GitHub Settings → Secrets → Actions |

---

That’s it! 🎉  
If you hit any snags (e.g., the repo has a different port, or you’re using a different registry), just tweak the values above accordingly. Happy coding!
